referees.quote: I therefore support its publication in Nature Communications. Below are several issues/comments for the authors to consider to further improve the clarity of this work

I recommend publication in Nature Communications after addressing the following concerns... Can the authors repeat the Fig. 3a experiment with the device flipped... A control experiment turning off the field above T_CDW is needed

the thermal-cycle measurements under a magnetic field performed in this study are not sufficient to identify breaking time-reversal symmetry in the CDW state. Therefore, I do not recommend the publication of the present paper in Nature Communications.

note: First round is Version 0; there is no sign of a transfer from another journal. R1 supports publication and frames its points as clarity improvements, so minor revision. R2 is a borderline call between minor and major revision. It recommends publication conditionally, but asks for new control experiments: in-situ device flipping after field training, removing the field above T_CDW, and R-T curves. I classed this as major revision. R3's rejection is explicit. In later rounds R1 and R3 recommended publication, and R2 did so after a further round.
